suggestion: Publish a 'provisional, not certified' board alongside the empty one.
why: An empty table teaches nothing about the strategies; a board with the gates printed on every row shows the work without claiming skill.
options: A: keep the board empty. B: add a provisional board with gates in every row. C: provisional board behind a collapsed section.
cost: One page change; no new data.
risk: A provisional board invites being read as a ranking if the gates are skimmed.

suggestion: Capture a second operator's close for the same 14 games.
why: A consensus close is far more defensible than one book's, and it makes the CLV measure robust to a single operator's movement.
options: A: stay single-provider. B: add FanDuel closes. C: add a third book.
risk: Two operators can disagree on the line, not just the vig; the rule for which close is 'the' close has to be chosen first.

why: The sample floor is 100 bets; nine weeks of 14 games is enough to reach it in one step instead of waiting a season.
options: A: wait for weeks to accumulate. B: backfill from the operator's historical endpoint if it is available. C: backfill from a licensed archive.
cost: A research pass; the feed must still stamp close_status per row.
risk: Historical closes are only trustworthy if the archive is the operator's own. A third-party archive would have to be labelled as such, not as verified.
recommendation: B, if the operator publishes history; otherwise C with an explicit source class.

suggestion: Make the depth page cover all 32 clubs.
why: Two clubs is a demonstration, not coverage. The injury question is league-wide.
options: A: leave at two clubs. B: read the other 30 published charts. C: find an official feed.
cost: A read per club, per week.
risk: 30 clubs is 30 different page formats; the parser will be fragile and every row must stay flagged unofficial.
recommendation: B, with C preferred if an official feed exists.

suggestion: Add opponent-adjusted ratings to the model.
why: The current rating is naive and its disagreements with the close are mostly its own error.
options: A: keep naive ratings. B: add a simple opponent adjustment. C: fit a full model with a declared window.
cost: One modelling pass plus a validation rerun.
risk: Any fitting on 137 games will overfit; the fit window must be declared before the numbers are seen.
recommendation: B, because it is defensible at this sample size.

suggestion: Add a per-team rest column from an official source.
why: Rest differential is the most-cited public signal and it is currently uncomputable.
options: A: leave it uncomputable. B: derive it from official game dates with Thursday/Monday handled explicitly. C: find a publisher that states rest days.
risk: Derivation is an inference, so it cannot be labelled verified; it would have to carry its own status.

suggestion: Capture official player-level stat lines for prop markets.
why: Unblocks S7 and every prop combo, which is a third of the brief's requested structures.
options: A: skip props. B: capture official box scores per game. C: licensed stats feed.
risk: Box-score parsing is the most error-prone step in the whole pack; it needs its own reconciliation gate.
recommendation: B, gated like the results feed.

suggestion: Add a promotion gate to mirror the demotion gate.
why: The demotion path exists; the promotion path is currently 'clear the gates', which does not say what happens after a demotion.
options: A: keep the current implicit path. B: publish explicit promotion criteria with the same numeric style as D1-D6.

suggestion: Expose the reconciliation as a build gate in CI.
why: A results feed that cannot silently drift is worth more than one that is checked by hand.
options: A: manual check. B: add a CI workflow that fails on any mismatch.
risk: CI minutes and a new shared file that another session may also want to touch.
recommendation: B, scoped to this pack's paths only.

suggestion: Publish a monthly decision review page.
why: Suggestions and flags accumulate faster than they are decided; a review cadence keeps the review gate real.
options: A: no cadence. B: monthly review page generated from the open rows.
risk: A cadence nobody keeps is worse than none.
recommendation: B, only after the first decision is actually taken.
